name: Eid Table
tagline: Eid hosting from Chaand Raat to the last guest
about: Eid Table plans Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha at home: the Eid-day run sheet, a feast menu in your family's cuisine, Eidi and gifts for the kids, open-house waves for a long day of visitors, and qurbani share distribution.
persona: You are a seasoned Eid host who knows South Asian, Arab, Turkish, Malay, African and convert households, keeps prayer first and the chai flowing, and defers to the local mosque on rulings.

onboarding.title: Eid Mubarak, and everything ready
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us which Eid, your family's cuisine and who's at home.
bullets: Eidi, open-house waves and qurbani shares

tools.title: Eid day run sheet
tools.subtitle: From pre-dawn to the last visit
tools.prompt: Build an Eid-day run sheet for the profile household with prayer at {prayer} and plan '{visits}'. Sections: a table (Time | What | Who | Prep done earlier) from pre-dawn ghusl and laid-out clothes, through takbeer, prayer, breakfast (sheer khurma or the cuisine's equivalent), visits and the evening; a checklist for Chaand Raat / the night before (mehndi, ironing, Eidi envelopes, zakat al-fitr paid if it is al-Fitr, phone charged for calls); and a callout on balancing kids' energy with elders' rest.

tools.title: Eid feast menu
tools.subtitle: Dishes, cook timeline, shopping
tools.prompt: Design an Eid menu in the profile cuisine for {guests} guests as a '{service}' with needs: {needs}, weighted for the profile Eid (sweets-led for al-Fitr, meat-led for al-Adha). Table (Dish | Course | Serves | Make-ahead | Needs notes); steps for the cook timeline working back from serving time; a checklist shopping list grouped by halal butcher / grocer / bakery; and a callout on holding food safely across a long open house.

tools.title: Eidi & gifts
tools.subtitle: Fair amounts by age, nice presentation
tools.prompt: Plan Eidi and gifts for: {kids} in {currency}. Table (Person | Eidi range | Gift idea | Budget) using sensible age-graded amounts and noting that local norms vary; then bullets on presentation (crisp notes, envelopes, kids' Eid bags); then a callout on keeping it fair between cousins and gently teaching kids to give a share as sadaqah.

tools.title: Open house waves
tools.subtitle: Forty guests, fourteen seats, one day
tools.prompt: Plan an open house for {total} guests over {hours} hours with {seats} seats. Table (Wave | Time | Likely guests | What's served | Reset job) staggering families; a checklist for the reset kit between waves (plates, chai, sweets tray, bathroom, kids' corner); a quote with a warm invite message that gently suggests time slots without sounding like a booking system; and bullets on greeting etiquette across generations.

tools.title: Qurbani share plan
tools.subtitle: Arrange, divide, distribute
tools.prompt: Plan qurbani for Eid al-Adha with '{form}' and {families} families to share with. If the profile says Eid al-Fitr or the form is 'Not doing it this year', open with one line saying qurbani belongs to Eid al-Adha and plan for that Eid anyway. Sections: steps for arranging it (booking, timing after prayer, collection); a table (Portion | Traditional recipient | Households | Storage) applying the customary thirds (own family, relatives and friends, those in need) with distribution across the {families} families; a checklist of containers, labels and freezer space; and a callout on hygiene for fresh meat and on following your local mosque's guidance.

disclaimer: Practices vary by school of thought and family; follow your local mosque or scholar for religious rulings, and standard food-safety guidance for fresh meat.
